docs.title: How COGANT assigns roles
docs.text:
What this page is: An explanation of COGANT's semantic rule engine — how rules fire on graph evidence, how conflicts are resolved, and what the Active Inference plus supporting evidence roles mean.

Prerequisites: Program graphs in COGANT and the role vocabulary from Active Inference.

Reading time: ~14 minutes

Next steps: Markov blankets in codebases · Tutorial: Writing a custom translation rule · The forward-reverse cycle

COGANT's rule engine is the component that looks at a program graph and decides: "This function is an observation. That class is hidden state. This validator is a constraint." This page explains the engine, the rule families, how conflicts are resolved, and how core roles differ from supporting evidence roles.

docs.title: The rule engine
docs.text:
The engine lives in py/cogant/translate/engine.py. It takes a ProgramGraph and a list of TranslationRule instances, runs every rule against every node, collects the resulting SemanticMapping records, and resolves conflicts when multiple rules fire on the same node.

Each rule implements two methods:

  • matches(graph, query) -- returns a list of matched patterns (node IDs + evidence)
  • apply(graph, match) -- converts a match into a SemanticMapping with a confidence score, provenance, and a MappingKind label

Rules also carry a priority and a confidence_score. When two rules assign different roles to the same code fragment, the engine picks the one with the higher (priority, confidence_score) tuple. This is how COGANT handles ambiguity: a function named handle_request triggers both ActionRule (keyword "handle") and PolicyRule (keyword "handle"), and the conflict is resolved by whichever rule produces stronger evidence.

docs.title: The five rule families
docs.text: Rules are organized into five families, each in its own module under py/cogant/translate/rules/:

docs.title: Structural rules (structural.py)
docs.text:
These rules look at graph topology -- edges, degree, containment -- without reading node names.

Rule Fires when Produces Confidence ReadOnlyInputRule Module has READS edges, zero WRITES OBSERVATION 0.70 MutatingSubsystemRule Class has any WRITES/MUTATES edge HIDDEN_STATE 0.75 InheritanceRule Class has INHERITS edges POLICY (if base is Abstract/Handler) 0.70 ContainmentRule Class contains 5+ methods Majority vote across method names 0.75 DataPipelineRule Function reads from A, writes to B (A != B) DATA_FLOW 0.75

docs.title: Semantic rules (semantic.py)
docs.text:
These rules match on function/class names using curated keyword lists.

Rule Keywords Produces Confidence ObservationRule get, read, fetch, query, display, show, status, info, list OBSERVATION 0.85 (keyword) / 0.70 (edge-only) ActionRule set, update, create, delete, send, push, execute, run, process, handle, dispatch ACTION 0.80 PolicyRule middleware, handler, controller, manager, router, dispatcher, scheduler POLICY 0.80 PreferenceRule validate, check, test_, assert_, Validator, Checker CONSTRAINT 0.85 ContextRule config, settings, env, options, params CONTEXT 0.80

docs.title: Behavioral rules (behavioral.py)
docs.text:
These rules detect runtime patterns from graph structure.

Rule Fires when Produces Confidence OrchestratorRule Node has 3+ outgoing CALLS edges ORCHESTRATION 0.80 TestAssertionRule Function name contains "test" + has CALLS edges CONSTRAINT 0.85 EventBusRule Node kind is EVENT with subscribers OBSERVATION 0.75

docs.title: Control rules (control.py)
docs.text:
These rules detect configuration and feature management.

Rule Fires when Produces Confidence ConfigRule Node kind is CONFIGURATION CONTEXT 0.90 FeatureFlagRule Node kind is FEATURE_FLAG CONTEXT 0.85 ParameterRule Tunable numeric/string constants CONTEXT 0.80

docs.title: Resilience rules (resilience.py)
docs.text:
These rules detect error handling and fault tolerance patterns.

Rule Fires when Produces Confidence RetryPatternRule Name contains retry, backoff, circuit, breaker, timeout, fallback POLICY 0.70 ErrorBoundaryRule Function has CATCHES or THROWS edges ERROR_HANDLING 0.70 SingletonAccessRule Variable/class read by 3+ modules across 3+ paths CONTEXT 0.65 CircuitBreakerRule Has GUARDS edge + retry keyword/metadata CIRCUIT_BREAKER 0.80

docs.title: How rules fire: a worked example
docs.text:
Consider this Python class:

class UserService:
    def __init__(self):
        self._cache = {}           # MutatingSubsystemRule fires (WRITES edge)

    def get_user(self, id: str):   # ObservationRule fires (keyword "get")
        return self._cache.get(id)

    def update_user(self, id, data):  # ActionRule fires (keyword "update")
        self._cache[id] = data

    def validate_user(self, data):    # PreferenceRule fires (keyword "validate")
        assert "email" in data

The engine produces four mappings:

  1. UserService -> HIDDEN_STATE (confidence 0.75, from MutatingSubsystemRule)
  2. get_user -> OBSERVATION (confidence 0.85, from ObservationRule keyword match)
  3. update_user -> ACTION (confidence 0.80, from ActionRule keyword match)
  4. validate_user -> CONSTRAINT (confidence 0.85, from PreferenceRule keyword match)

If ContainmentRule also fires on UserService (it has methods), the majority-vote classification at confidence 0.75 is resolved against the per-method rules which carry higher confidence. The per-method mappings win.

docs.title: HIDDEN_STATE
docs.text: Internal mutable state that is not directly observable from outside. Private fields, caches, buffers, accumulators. In the GNN output, these become StateSpaceBlock variables. In the Markov blanket, these are internal nodes. Detected by MutatingSubsystemRule — see translation rules reference and semantic roles reference.

docs.title: OBSERVATION
docs.text: Read-only access points that expose hidden state. Getter methods, query functions, logging handlers. These become observation modalities in the GNN and feed the A (likelihood) matrix. Detected by ObservationRule and ReadOnlyInputRule — see translation rules reference.

docs.title: ACTION
docs.text: Functions that change hidden state. Setters, mutators, event publishers, request handlers. These become action variables in the GNN and define the B (transition) matrix slices. Detected by ActionRule — see translation rules reference.

docs.title: POLICY
docs.text: Control logic that selects which action to execute. Controllers, routers, schedulers, retry strategies. These map to the policy layer in Active Inference -- the mechanism that minimizes expected free energy. Detected by PolicyRule, InheritanceRule, and RetryPatternRule — see translation rules reference.

docs.title: PREFERENCE
docs.text: Explicit preference evidence over observations. The MappingKind exists in the schema and in GNN import/export vocabulary; the shipped source-code rule set usually represents validators and tests as CONSTRAINT mappings rather than emitting a standalone PREFERENCE mapping.

docs.title: CONSTRAINT
docs.text: Validators and tests that define what the system considers correct. Assertions, schema validators, type checkers. These populate the C (preference) matrix in the GNN. Detected by PreferenceRule and TestAssertionRule — see translation rules reference.

docs.title: CONTEXT
docs.text: Configuration, feature flags, and global state that parameterize the system. These populate the D (prior) matrix in the GNN -- the initial beliefs before any observations. Detected by ContextRule, ConfigRule, FeatureFlagRule, and SingletonAccessRule — see translation rules reference.

docs.title: DATA_FLOW
docs.text: Functions that read from one source and write to a different target. Transformation pipelines, ETL functions, adapters. These appear in the Connections section of the GNN. Detected by DataPipelineRule — see translation rules reference.

docs.title: Supporting evidence roles
docs.text: DATA_FLOW, ERROR_HANDLING, ORCHESTRATION, and CIRCUIT_BREAKER are supporting roles in the current package. They are retained in mapping JSON, provenance, dashboards, and evidence traces because they explain graph structure and conflict resolution, but they are not separate A/B/C/D state-space axes in the way HIDDEN_STATE, OBSERVATION, and ACTION are.

docs.title: Confidence tiers
docs.text:
Every mapping carries a ConfidenceTier label:

  • STATIC_ONLY -- based purely on static analysis (all current rules)
  • STATIC_PLUS_RUNTIME -- static + dynamic trace evidence (e.g., EventBusRule)
  • RUNTIME_ONLY -- dynamic evidence only (future)
  • HUMAN_REVIEWED -- manually approved (future)

The confidence score (0.65 to 0.90) determines conflict resolution priority. ConfigRule at 0.90 is the highest confidence in the entire family -- explicit configuration is ground truth. SingletonAccessRule at 0.65 is the lowest -- "read by many modules" is a weak signal.

docs.text:

docs.title: The forward-reverse cycle
docs.text:
What this page is: A conceptual overview of COGANT's bidirectional pipeline — code-to-GNN, GNN-to-code, and the round-trip that closes the loop with diff-based equivalence checks.

Prerequisites: What is a GNN?, How COGANT assigns roles.

Reading time: ~10 minutes

Next steps: Tutorial: Reverse mode — GNN to code · Markov blankets in codebases · Active Inference for programmers

COGANT's most ambitious claim is that the mapping between source code and Active Inference models is not one-way. The forward pipeline translates code into a GNN. The reverse pipeline synthesizes code back from a GNN. Together they form a cycle:

code --forward--> GNN --reverse--> code'

This page explains both directions, the role-preservation score, and the stricter invariant ledger that determines the current v0.6 roundtrip status.

docs.title: Forward: code to GNN
docs.text:
The forward pipeline is a six-layer evidence transformation:

  1. Source to graph. Tree-sitter or the Python AST front end parses source code, then COGANT's graph builder extracts a typed program graph with nodes (MODULE, CLASS, FUNCTION, METHOD, VARIABLE) and edges (CALLS, READS, WRITES, IMPORTS, CONTAINS). The graph preserves the relationships the front end extracts; whitespace, comments, unsupported constructs, and dynamic effects remain outside the graph unless a later stage adds evidence.

  2. Graph to semantic mappings. The rule engine runs 22 translation rules against the graph. Each rule that fires produces a SemanticMapping with a confidence score. Conflicts are resolved by (priority, confidence) ordering.

  3. Mappings to state space. The state-space compiler projects the role assignments onto an ordered basis of hidden states, observations, and actions. Each basis element corresponds to a node in the graph.

  4. State space to A/B/C/D matrices. The matrix builder counts evidence edges and normalizes to produce well-formed probability distributions. The result is a complete Active Inference model.

  5. Matrices to GNN markdown. The GNNMarkdownFormatter emits a valid upstream GNN v2.0.0-engine file with the required StateSpaceBlock, Connections, InitialParameterization, Equations, Time, ActInfOntologyAnnotation, ModelParameters, Footer, and Signature sections.

  6. GNN package. The GNNPackageBuilder writes model.gnn.md, model.gnn.json, satellite matrix files, the Markov blanket partition, and provenance metadata into a self-contained directory.

Each stage is traceable: the output records the source artifact, rule evidence, fallback paths, and validation status needed to inspect what was preserved and what was approximated. The GNN file is not a behavioral proof of the source code; it is a structured export of the extracted program graph, semantic mappings, state-space model, and matrix defaults.

docs.title: Reverse: GNN to code
docs.text:
The reverse pipeline reads a GNN package and synthesizes a Python package that, when analyzed by a forward run, is compared against the original GNN through the v0.6 invariant ledger. The implementation in py/cogant/reverse/ is exposed through the cogant reverse and cogant roundtrip CLI subcommands and emits POLICY / CONTEXT scaffolding proportional to the origin GNN's role counts:

# doctest: +SKIP  # requires a pre-generated GNN package on disk
from pathlib import Path
from cogant.gnn.runner import load_gnn_package
from cogant.simulate.runner import SimulationRunner

# Load a forward-produced GNN package
gnn = load_gnn_package(Path("output/calculator/gnn_package"))

# The matrices define the synthesized package's behavior
print("Hidden states:", [s.name for s in gnn.state_space.variables.values()])
# ['display', 'accumulator', 'history_len']

print("Observations:", [o.name for o in gnn.state_space.observations.values()])
# ['get_display', 'get_history', 'assert_display']

print("Actions:", [a.name for a in gnn.state_space.actions.values()])
# ['_execute_operation']

The synthesized code' has:

  • One class per hidden-state cluster (each mutable attribute group becomes a class)
  • One method per action (each ACTION mapping becomes a method that writes to the state variables it is connected to in the B matrix)
  • One getter per observation (each OBSERVATION mapping becomes a read-only method)
  • Module-level constants for preferences and priors (C and D vectors)

The synthesized code is not a copy of the original -- it is a minimal implementation that preserves the generative model structure. Variable names come from the GNN labels, not the original source.

docs.title: The roundtrip measure
docs.text:
How do you know the roundtrip worked? COGANT defines the role-preservation fidelity metric as:

s_role = mean_role min(count_original[role], count_resynthesized[role])
                / max(count_original[role], count_resynthesized[role])

where the mean ranges over every role present in either the original or resynthesized bundle. A perfect role-preservation score has s_role = 1.0 (the two role multisets match exactly), and the public ROLE_PRESERVED threshold is s_role >= 0.5. Because the denominator is per-role max(original, resynthesized), the score penalizes both dropped roles and extra roles introduced by the synthesizer; it is not a recall ratio.

The v0.6 invariant ledger separately checks stronger properties:

  1. State-space shape preservation — same hidden-state, observation, and action dimensions.
  2. A/B/C/D matrix preservation — same matrix shapes and value deltas within tolerance.
  3. GNN-section preservation — same required section coverage and comparable section content.
  4. Program-graph preservation — same node/edge counts and edge-kind distributions.
  5. Generated-code health — synthesized package imports, compiles, and passes smoke checks.

Strict STRUCTURALLY_ISOMORPHIC status requires those ledger checks in addition to role preservation (canonical source cogant/evaluation/METRICS.yaml).

Compatibility note: Earlier drafts used a complementary "error" formulation in ISOMORPHISM_THEOREM.md, where ε_max = 0 meant exact recovery. The current project-wide convention is the symmetric role-overlap score above, where 1.0 is exact.

In practice, the forward pipeline discards information that cannot be recovered:

  • Whitespace and comments are lost at stage 1 (AST extraction)
  • Dead code that has no edges in the program graph is invisible to the rule engine
  • Name choices are preserved as labels but the synthesizer may normalize them
  • Control flow ordering within a function body is not captured by the graph

These losses explain why role preservation can pass while stricter graph, matrix, or generated-code invariants fail. Treat ROLE_PRESERVED as a useful semantic-regression tier and STRUCTURALLY_ISOMORPHIC as the strict tier.

docs.title: Galois Connection Framing
docs.text:
The theory sketch frames the forward and reverse pipelines as a restricted Galois-style relation between two partially ordered sets:

  • Programs, ordered by behavioral refinement (P1 refines P2 if P1 can do everything P2 can do)
  • Generative models, ordered by model inclusion (M1 includes M2 if M1's state space contains M2's)

The forward pipeline F is the lower adjoint: it maps a program to the smallest generative model that captures its structure. The reverse pipeline R is the upper adjoint: it maps a generative model to the largest program that is consistent with it.

Under that restricted role-quotient reading, the intended equations are:

F(R(F(code))) = F(code)     -- forward is idempotent after one roundtrip
R(F(R(gnn)))  = R(gnn)      -- reverse is idempotent after one roundtrip

The current package does not use "epsilon-isomorphism" as a CLI or manuscript success tier. It reports roundtrip_status, role_preservation_score, and the invariant ledger described above.

docs.title: A concrete GNN roundtrip example
docs.text:
Given the Calculator fixture, forward analysis produces a GNN with:

## StateSpaceBlock
- s_f0: display (int, cardinality=10)
- s_f1: accumulator (float, cardinality=1)

## ActInfOntologyAnnotation
- display: HiddenState
- get_display: Observation
- _execute_operation: Action

Reverse synthesis produces a Python package with:

class CalculatorModel:
    """Synthesized from GNN StateSpaceBlock."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.display: int = 0         # s_f0
        self.accumulator: float = 0.0  # s_f1

    def get_display(self) -> int:
        """Observation modality for display."""
        return self.display

    def execute_operation(self, op: str, value: float):
        """Action: transitions display and accumulator."""
        self.accumulator = self.accumulator  # B matrix placeholder
        self.display = self.display          # B matrix placeholder

Running cogant translate on this synthesized code produces a GNN whose StateSpaceBlock dimensions, A matrix non-zero pattern, and blanket partition can be inspected by the roundtrip invariant ledger.

docs.title: Current limitations
docs.text:
• cogant reverse and cogant roundtrip are available CLI subcommands in v0.6.0.
  • Only Python synthesis output is supported.
  • The B matrix placeholder code does not implement real transition logic -- it preserves the structural skeleton.
  • Complex control flow (loops, conditionals, exception handling) is not synthesized.

docs.title: COGANT Cookbook
docs.text: Practical recipes for common COGANT workflows. Each recipe is self-contained, takes 2-15 minutes to complete, and ships with copy-pasteable commands. Use the cookbook when you have a specific outcome in mind; use ../tutorials/ when you want a guided walkthrough and ../concepts/ when you want background theory.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text: # Recipe Description Level 01 Scan your first project Run cogant scan on a Python repo and read the summary table Beginner 02 Export as JSON Pipe the program graph into a JSON file for downstream tools Beginner 03 Explain a node Understand why a node was assigned its Active Inference role Beginner 04 Custom thresholds Tune confidence thresholds via pipeline config YAML Intermediate 05 Monorepo scanning Run COGANT across multiple packages in a monorepo Intermediate 06 Reverse synthesis Generate a runnable Python package from a GNN markdown file Intermediate 07 Custom package layout Control the output directory and structure of synthesized code Intermediate 08 CI/CD integration Add COGANT validation to a GitHub Actions workflow Intermediate 09 Pre-commit hook Detect GNN drift before commits land Intermediate 10 Docker Run COGANT inside a container for reproducible builds Intermediate 11 JavaScript/TypeScript Scan JS/TS projects alongside Python Intermediate 12 Batch scanning Translate many repos in a single shell loop Intermediate 13 Incremental rescanning Skip unchanged files with cogant changed Intermediate 14 GNN validation Validate a hand-written or edited GNN package Intermediate 15 Markov blanket visualization Visualize blanket partitions in the program graph Intermediate 16 PNG export Rasterize Mermaid/SVG/dot diagrams to PNG Beginner 17 Benchmarking Measure pipeline wall-clock performance Advanced 18 Role filtering Filter results by semantic role using jq Intermediate 19 Custom translation rules Add a new rule to the translation engine Advanced 20 Dataset export Export a training dataset for ML from COGANT output Advanced

docs.title: Numbering scheme
docs.text: Recipes are numbered NN_slug.md roughly in the order a new user is likely to encounter them: basics first (01-05), then integration and workflow (06-13), then the more advanced workflows (14-20). Numbers are editorial only — they do not encode dependencies, and you can jump to any recipe directly.

docs.title: Non-numbered recipes
docs.text:
Three stable recipes predate the numbering scheme and are kept under their original slugs so external links do not break. They remain valid but new content should go into a new numbered recipe rather than extending these.

Recipe Description Status Analyze a Flask app End-to-end Flask analysis walkthrough Stable; overlaps with ../tutorials/03_flask_walkthrough.md Custom translation rules Author a new translation rule for the engine Stable; overlaps with 19_extend_rules.md Interpret GNN output Read and interpret a generated GNN package Stable; overlaps with 03_explain_node.md

docs.title: Recommended Reading Order
docs.text:
1. 01 Scan your first project — confirm COGANT works end-to-end on your machine.
  2. 02 Export as JSON and 03 Explain a node — learn to read and interrogate the output.
  3. 04 Custom thresholds — your first configuration tweak.
  4. 08 CI/CD integration and 09 Pre-commit hook — wire COGANT into your day-to-day workflow.
  5. 06 Reverse synthesis and 14 GNN validation — exercise the reverse pipeline and validation surface.
  6. Pick targeted recipes from the rest of the table as use cases arise.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
All recipes assume COGANT is installed:

pip install cogant
# or with visualization extras
pip install "cogant[viz]"

Verify your environment:

cogant doctor

Agent notes: AGENTS.md - Hub: ../index.md

docs.title: Recipe 1: How to Scan Your First Python Project
docs.text: Goal: Run cogant scan on a local Python repository and read the summary table. Time: ~2 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed (pip install cogant)
  • A Python project directory on disk

docs.title: 1. Verify the environment
docs.text:
cogant doctor

All checks should pass. If any fail, install the missing dependency listed in the diagnostic output.

docs.title: 2. Initialize COGANT in the project (optional)
docs.text:
cogant init ./my-project --check

This creates a .cogant/config.json scaffold and optionally runs environment diagnostics. Safe to skip if you only want a quick scan.

docs.title: 3. Scan the project
docs.text:
cogant scan ./my-project

COGANT runs static-analysis extractors (AST parsing, type inference, symbol tables) and prints a Rich table:

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
Scanning ./my-project
┌──────────────────────┬──────────┐
│ Property             │ Value    │
├──────────────────────┼──────────┤
│ Target               │ ./my-p…  │
│ Type                 │ python   │
│ Files (ingest)       │ 42       │
│ Python modules parsed│ 38       │
│ Symbol summary       │ 38       │
└──────────────────────┴──────────┘

docs.title: 4. Get JSON instead of a table
docs.text:
cogant scan ./my-project --format json

This prints the raw analysis result as JSON, useful for piping into jq or other tools.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Error: Repository not found Check the path exists and is a directory Files (ingest): 0 Ensure the directory contains .py, .js, or .ts files Permission denied Check file read permissions on the repo

docs.title: Recipe 2: Exporting Program Graph as JSON
docs.text: Goal: Translate a repository and export the program graph as a JSON file. Time: ~5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A Python or JS/TS project directory

docs.title: 1. Run the full translation pipeline
docs.text:
cogant translate ./my-project --output ./cogant-output

This runs all pipeline stages (ingest, static, normalize, graph, translate, statespace, process, export, validate) and writes bundle.json to the output directory.

docs.title: 2. Inspect the bundle
docs.text:
cat ./cogant-output/bundle.json | python3 -m json.tool | head -40

The bundle contains target, artifacts, stage_results, errors, and metadata keys.

docs.title: 3. Re-export in JSON-only format
docs.text:
If you already have a bundle and want a clean re-export:

cogant export-gnn ./cogant-output/bundle.json --output ./export --format json

docs.title: 4. Extract the program graph with jq
docs.text: jq '.stage_results.graph' ./cogant-output/bundle.json > program_graph.json

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
Exporting ./cogant-output/bundle.json
 JSON  ./export/bundle.json

 Export complete

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix bundle.json is empty Check cogant translate completed without errors stage_results.graph is null The graph stage may have been skipped; run without --skip Large JSON file Use jq to extract only the keys you need

docs.title: Recipe 3: Explaining Why a Node Got Its Role
docs.text: Goal: Understand why COGANT assigned a specific Active Inference role to a node. Time: ~3 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A Python project with at least a few modules

docs.title: 1. Scan first to discover node names
docs.text:
cogant scan ./my-project --format json | jq '.modules[].name'

Pick a module or symbol name from the output.

docs.title: 2. Explain the node
docs.text:
cogant explain ./my-project UserService

COGANT runs the static pipeline (ingest through translate), resolves UserService to a concrete node, and queries every translation rule for whether it fired.

docs.title: 3. Get JSON output for scripting
docs.text:
cogant explain ./my-project UserService --format json

The JSON includes rules_fired, semantic_kind, markov_blanket_role, and edges for each rule that considered the node.

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
Explaining node: UserService

Rule                  Status     Kind           Role
────────────────────────────────────────────────────
class_with_state      FIRED      hidden_state   mu
method_calls_extern   considered observation    --
imports_io_module     FIRED      sensory        eta

Markov blanket role: mu (internal state)
Confidence: 0.87

docs.title: 4. Explain with a substring match
docs.text:
You do not need the full node name. A substring works:

cogant explain ./my-project "User"

COGANT resolves the closest matching node.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Node not found (exit code 2) Check spelling; use cogant scan --format json to list nodes Pipeline error (exit code 1) Ensure the repo path is correct and contains source files Multiple matches Provide a more specific substring to disambiguate

docs.title: Recipe 4: Tuning Confidence Thresholds
docs.text: Goal: Adjust the translation confidence thresholds via a pipeline config file. Time: ~5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A Python project directory

docs.title: 1. Create a pipeline config file
docs.text:
cat > cogant-config.yaml << 'EOF'
pipeline:
  stages:
    - ingest
    - static
    - normalize
    - graph
    - translate
    - statespace
    - process
    - export
    - validate
  plugins:
    translate:
      confidence_threshold: 0.65
      min_evidence_edges: 2
EOF

The confidence_threshold controls how confident a translation rule must be before assigning a role. Lower values produce more assignments but with more noise; higher values are stricter.

docs.title: 2. Run translate with the config
docs.text: cogant translate ./my-project --config cogant-config.yaml --output ./output-tuned

docs.title: 3. Compare against the default threshold
docs.text:
Run a second translation with defaults:

cogant translate ./my-project --output ./output-default

Then diff the two runs:

cogant diff ./output-default ./output-tuned

docs.title: 4. Iterate
docs.text:
Adjust confidence_threshold in the YAML and re-run. Common ranges:

Threshold Behavior 0.3 - 0.5 Aggressive: more nodes assigned, more false positives 0.5 - 0.7 Balanced (default range) 0.7 - 0.9 Conservative: fewer assignments, higher precision

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text: The cogant diff output shows which nodes gained or lost role assignments between the two runs, along with an architectural drift score.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Warning: failed to load config Check YAML syntax; ensure pipeline: is the top-level key All nodes unassigned Threshold is too high; lower it to 0.5 Too many noisy assignments Raise the threshold or increase min_evidence_edges

docs.title: Recipe 5: Running COGANT on a Monorepo
docs.text: Goal: Translate multiple packages inside a single monorepo. Time: ~10 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A monorepo with several Python or JS/TS packages

docs.title: 1. Identify the packages
docs.text:
ls -d ./monorepo/packages/*/

Assume the layout is:

monorepo/
  packages/
    auth/
    billing/
    gateway/

docs.title: 2. Initialize each package
docs.text:
for pkg in ./monorepo/packages/*/; do
  cogant init "$pkg" --quiet
done

docs.title: 3. Translate each package independently
docs.text:
for pkg in ./monorepo/packages/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$pkg")
  echo "--- Translating $name ---"
  cogant translate "$pkg" --output "./output/$name"
done

Each package gets its own output directory with a separate bundle.json.

docs.title: 4. Validate all outputs
docs.text:
for dir in ./output/*/; do
  echo "--- Validating $(basename "$dir") ---"
  cogant validate "$dir"
done

docs.title: 5. Compare packages pairwise (optional)
docs.text: cogant diff ./output/auth ./output/billing

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text: Each package produces a pipeline summary table and a bundle.json. The diff command shows structural differences between packages, which is useful for detecting shared patterns or drift across services.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Some packages fail with 0 files Ensure each directory contains source files; check .cogant/config.json target path Shared code not resolved COGANT scans each directory independently; shared libraries need their own scan Output directories collide Use --output "./output/$(basename $pkg)" to namespace by package

docs.title: Recipe 6: Generating Code from a GNN
docs.text: Goal: Synthesize a runnable Python package from a GNN markdown file. Time: ~3 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A GNN markdown file (produced by cogant translate or written by hand)

docs.title: 1. Locate your GNN file
docs.text:
After running cogant translate, find the GNN markdown in the output:

find ./output -name "model.gnn.md" -type f

docs.title: 2. Run reverse synthesis
docs.text:
cogant reverse ./output/gnn_package/model.gnn.md --output ./synthesized

COGANT parses the GNN, plans the package layout, and emits:

  • One Factor<N> class per hidden-state slot
  • observe_<name> functions for each observation modality
  • act_<name> functions for each action
  • A select_policy helper
  • check_<name> predicates for each constraint
  • Runtime A/B/C/D matrices in matrices.py

docs.title: 3. Inspect the synthesized package
docs.text: ls ./synthesized/

docs.title: 4. Get a JSON summary instead of the Rich table
docs.text: cogant reverse ./output/gnn_package/model.gnn.md --output ./synthesized --json

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
Synthesized package: ./synthesized/my_project_gnn/
  Hidden states:  4
  Observations:   3
  Actions:        2
  Policies:       1
  Constraints:    2
  Matrices:       A, B, C, D

docs.title: 5. Verify roundtrip preservation
docs.text:
cogant roundtrip ./output/gnn_package/model.gnn.md --keep-tmp

This forward-translates the synthesized package and checks the current roundtrip taxonomy: strict structural isomorphism when all invariant-ledger checks pass, ROLE_PRESERVED when semantic roles survive but structure drifts, and DRIFT / FAILED for weaker outcomes. For day-to-day reverse work, inspect role_preservation_score and the invariant table rather than treating a role-only match as structural isomorphism.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Error during synthesis Check the GNN file is valid markdown with the expected section headers Missing matrix files The GNN may not define all four matrices; this is expected for simple models Round-trip score below threshold Complex repos may have information loss; inspect --keep-tmp output to debug

docs.title: Recipe 7: Customizing Synthesized Package Layout
docs.text: Goal: Control the output directory and structure of reverse-synthesized code. Time: ~5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A GNN markdown file

docs.title: 1. Choose your output directory
docs.text:
cogant reverse ./model.gnn.md --output ./my-custom-output

The --output flag sets the root directory. COGANT creates a named subdirectory inside it based on the GNN model name.

docs.title: 2. Examine the default structure
docs.text:
tree ./my-custom-output/

Typical layout:

my-custom-output/
  my_project_gnn/
    __init__.py
    factors.py
    observations.py
    actions.py
    policies.py
    constraints.py
    matrices.py

docs.title: 3. Verify the package is importable
docs.text:
cd ./my-custom-output
python3 -c "import my_project_gnn; print(dir(my_project_gnn))"

docs.title: 4. Feed the synthesized package back into COGANT
docs.text:
cogant translate ./my-custom-output/my_project_gnn --output ./re-translated

This closes the loop: GNN to code to GNN.

docs.title: 5. Compare the original and re-translated GNN
docs.text: cogant diff ./original-output ./re-translated

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text: The re-translated bundle should produce a GNN structurally similar to the original, with high role-match score from cogant roundtrip.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Output directory already exists COGANT overwrites files; use a fresh directory if you need to preserve existing output Package not importable Check __init__.py exists; ensure no syntax errors in generated code Drift between original and re-translated Expected for large models; inspect per-node diffs with cogant explain

docs.title: Recipe 8: Using COGANT in CI/CD (GitHub Actions)
docs.text: Goal: Add COGANT translation and validation to a GitHub Actions workflow. Time: ~10 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A GitHub repository
  • COGANT available on PyPI or installable from source

docs.title: 1. Create the workflow file
docs.text: mkdir -p .github/workflows

docs.title: 2. Write the workflow
docs.text:
Create .github/workflows/cogant.yml:

name: COGANT Analysis

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  cogant:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install COGANT
        run: pip install cogant

      - name: Check environment
        run: cogant doctor

      - name: Translate repository
        run: cogant translate . --output ./cogant-output --no-dynamic

      - name: Validate GNN output
        run: cogant validate ./cogant-output

      - name: Upload artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: cogant-output
          path: ./cogant-output/
          retention-days: 30

docs.title: 3. Add baseline diffing for PRs (optional)
docs.text:
Extend the workflow to compare the PR branch against main:

      - name: Translate baseline (main)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: |
          git stash
          git checkout ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          cogant translate . --output ./cogant-baseline --no-dynamic
          git checkout -
          git stash pop || true

      - name: Diff against baseline
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: cogant diff ./cogant-baseline ./cogant-output -o drift-report.md

      - name: Comment drift report
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@v2
        with:
          path: drift-report.md

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text: The workflow produces a cogant-output artifact containing the full bundle, GNN package, and validation results. On PRs, the drift report is posted as a comment.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix cogant doctor fails Install missing system dependencies in the workflow Translate times out Add --no-dynamic to skip coverage/trace analysis; use --skip validate for speed Diff step fails Ensure both baseline and current outputs exist; check git checkout succeeded

docs.title: Recipe 9: Pre-commit Hook for GNN Drift Detection
docs.text: Goal: Detect GNN drift before commits land using a pre-commit hook. Time: ~5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A git repository with an existing COGANT baseline

docs.title: 1. Generate the baseline
docs.text:
Run a full translate on the current commit and save it:

cogant translate . --output .cogant/baseline --no-dynamic

Commit the baseline so it is available for comparison:

git add .cogant/baseline/
git commit -m "chore: add COGANT baseline"

docs.title: 2. Create the pre-commit hook
docs.text:
cat > .git/hooks/pre-commit << 'HOOK'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

# Only run if Python/JS/TS files changed
changed=$(cogant changed . --source-only 2>/dev/null)
if [ -z "$changed" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

echo "[cogant] Source files changed -- checking for GNN drift..."

# Translate the working tree
cogant translate . --output .cogant/current --no-dynamic 2>/dev/null

# Compare against baseline
drift_output=$(cogant diff .cogant/baseline .cogant/current 2>&1)
echo "$drift_output"

# Clean up
rm -rf .cogant/current

# Fail if drift report contains errors
if echo "$drift_output" | grep -q "INVALID"; then
  echo "[cogant] GNN drift detected -- review the diff above"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[cogant] No significant drift detected"
HOOK

chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit

docs.title: 3. Alternatively, use a .pre-commit-config.yaml entry
docs.text:
If you use the pre-commit framework:

repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: cogant-drift
        name: COGANT drift check
        entry: bash -c 'cogant translate . --output /tmp/cogant-check --no-dynamic && cogant validate /tmp/cogant-check && rm -rf /tmp/cogant-check'
        language: system
        types: [python]
        pass_filenames: false

docs.title: 4. Test the hook
docs.text:
echo "# test change" >> some_module.py
git add some_module.py
git commit -m "test: trigger drift check"

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
[cogant] Source files changed -- checking for GNN drift...
Diff complete
[cogant] No significant drift detected

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Hook is slow Add --skip validate or use --no-dynamic to reduce pipeline stages False positives Regenerate the baseline after intentional architectural changes Hook not running Check chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit

docs.title: Recipe 10: Running COGANT in Docker
docs.text: Goal: Run COGANT inside a container for reproducible, isolated builds. Time: ~10 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • Docker installed and running

docs.title: 1. Create a Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.11-slim

RUN pip install --no-cache-dir cogant

# For PNG export support, install viz extras and system deps
# RUN pip install --no-cache-dir "cogant[viz]" && \
#     apt-get update && apt-get install -y graphviz && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /workspace

ENTRYPOINT ["cogant"]
CMD ["--help"]

docs.title: 2. Build the image
docs.text: docker build -t cogant:latest .

docs.title: 3. Run a scan
docs.text:
Mount your project as a volume:

docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/my-project:/workspace/repo:ro" \
  cogant:latest scan /workspace/repo

docs.title: 4. Run the full pipeline
docs.text:
docker run --rm \
  -v "$(pwd)/my-project:/workspace/repo:ro" \
  -v "$(pwd)/output:/workspace/output" \
  cogant:latest translate /workspace/repo --output /workspace/output --no-dynamic

The output is written to ./output/ on the host.

docs.title: 5. Validate the output
docs.text:
docker run --rm \
  -v "$(pwd)/output:/workspace/output:ro" \
  cogant:latest validate /workspace/output

docs.title: 6. Run doctor inside the container
docs.text: docker run --rm cogant:latest doctor

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
COGANT Pipeline
Translating /workspace/repo to GNN...
...
 Translation complete
Output: /workspace/output

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Permission denied on output Ensure the output volume is writable: remove :ro from the output mount Missing graphviz for PNG Uncomment the apt-get install graphviz line in the Dockerfile Slow first run The image caches pip packages; subsequent builds are fast Dynamic analysis fails Mount coverage databases alongside the repo, or use --no-dynamic

docs.title: Recipe 11: Scanning JavaScript/TypeScript Projects
docs.text: Goal: Translate a JS/TS project into a GNN state-space model. Time: ~5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A JavaScript or TypeScript project directory

docs.title: 1. Check supported file types
docs.text:
COGANT parses these extensions: .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, .ts, .tsx

Verify your project has recognized files:

cogant scan ./my-js-project

The summary table shows the file count under "Files (ingest)".

docs.title: 2. Translate the project
docs.text:
cogant translate ./my-js-project --output ./js-output --no-dynamic

The --no-dynamic flag skips coverage/trace analysis, which currently requires Python-style .coverage databases. JS projects should use this flag unless you have a Cobertura coverage.xml.

docs.title: 3. Provide JS coverage data (optional)
docs.text:
If you have a Cobertura XML from Istanbul/nyc:

cogant translate ./my-js-project \
  --output ./js-output \
  --coverage ./my-js-project/coverage/cobertura-coverage.xml

docs.title: 4. Inspect the results
docs.text: cogant validate ./js-output

docs.title: 5. Mixed Python + JS monorepo
docs.text:
For a monorepo with both languages, scan the root:

cogant translate ./monorepo --output ./mono-output --no-dynamic

COGANT detects both Python and JS/TS files in a single pass.

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
Scanning ./my-js-project
┌──────────────────────┬──────────┐
│ Property             │ Value    │
├──────────────────────┼──────────┤
│ Target               │ ./my-j…  │
│ Type                 │ mixed    │
│ Files (ingest)       │ 87       │
│ Python modules parsed│ 0        │
│ Symbol summary       │ 87       │
└──────────────────────┴──────────┘

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix 0 files ingested Check file extensions match the supported set above node_modules included COGANT should ignore node_modules by default; check .cogant/config.json Low symbol count Complex TS generics may not fully parse; file an issue with a minimal repro

docs.title: Recipe 12: Batch-Scanning Multiple Repos
docs.text: Goal: Translate many repositories in a single shell loop and collect results. Time: ~10 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • Multiple repository directories (or a directory of cloned repos)

docs.title: 1. Organize your repos
docs.text:
repos/
  repo-alpha/
  repo-beta/
  repo-gamma/

docs.title: 2. Batch translate
docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

REPOS_DIR="./repos"
OUTPUT_DIR="./batch-output"
ERRORS=()

for repo in "$REPOS_DIR"/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$repo")
  echo "=== Translating $name ==="

  if cogant translate "$repo" --output "$OUTPUT_DIR/$name" --no-dynamic 2>&1; then
    echo "  OK: $name"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $name"
    ERRORS+=("$name")
  fi
done

echo ""
echo "=== Summary ==="
echo "Total: $(ls -d "$REPOS_DIR"/*/ | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
echo "Failed: ${#ERRORS[@]}"
for e in "${ERRORS[@]}"; do
  echo "  - $e"
done

docs.title: 3. Validate all outputs
docs.text:
for dir in ./batch-output/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$dir")
  echo "--- $name ---"
  cogant validate "$dir" || echo "  INVALID: $name"
done

docs.title: 4. Export a combined summary
docs.text:
for dir in ./batch-output/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$dir")
  echo "$name: $(jq '.errors | length' "$dir/bundle.json" 2>/dev/null || echo 'N/A') errors"
done

docs.title: 5. Run in parallel (GNU parallel)
docs.text:
ls -d ./repos/*/ | parallel -j4 \
  'name=$(basename {}); cogant translate {} --output ./batch-output/$name --no-dynamic'

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text: Each repo produces its own output directory with bundle.json and (if validation passes) a gnn_package/ subdirectory.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Some repos fail Check the error output; common causes are missing source files or permission issues Disk space Each output is typically 1-10 MB; clean up with rm -rf ./batch-output/*/ Slow on many repos Use GNU parallel (-j4) or xargs -P4 for concurrent runs

docs.title: Recipe 13: Incremental Rescanning (Skip Unchanged Files)
docs.text: Goal: Re-analyze only the files that changed since a previous run. Time: ~5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A git repository with a previous COGANT output

docs.title: 1. List changed files
docs.text:
cogant changed . --source-only

This compares against HEAD~1 by default. To compare against a specific ref:

cogant changed . --since main --source-only

docs.title: 2. Write the changed file list to disk
docs.text: cogant changed . --source-only --output changed-files.txt

docs.title: 3. List only Python changes
docs.text: cogant changed . --python-only

docs.title: 4. Full incremental workflow
docs.text:
Combine changed with translate for a focused re-run:

# Check if any source files changed
count=$(cogant changed . --source-only 2>&1 | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+')

if [ "$count" = "0" ]; then
  echo "No source files changed -- skipping re-translate"
else
  echo "$count files changed -- re-translating"
  cogant translate . --output ./output-incremental --no-dynamic
fi

docs.title: 5. Compare against previous output
docs.text: cogant diff ./output-previous ./output-incremental

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
3 source files changed since HEAD~1
  src/auth.py
  src/billing.py
  tests/test_auth.py

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Not a git repository (exit code 1) The directory must be inside a git working tree 0 files but changes exist Check the --since ref is correct; verify with git diff --name-only --python-only misses .pyi files .pyi files are included in --source-only but not --python-only

docs.title: Recipe 14: Validating a Hand-Written GNN Against AII Spec
docs.text: Goal: Run COGANT's GNN validator on a manually authored or edited GNN package. Time: ~3 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A GNN package directory containing at minimum manifest.json and model.gnn.md

docs.title: 1. Understand the expected structure
docs.text:
A valid GNN package directory looks like:

gnn_package/
  manifest.json
  model.gnn.md
  model.gnn.json     (optional)
  program_graph.json  (optional)
  semantic_mappings.json (optional)

docs.title: 2. Validate the package
docs.text:
cogant validate ./gnn_package

COGANT detects the manifest.json + model.gnn.md pair and runs the full GNNValidator, which checks:

  • Manifest schema conformance
  • GNN markdown section structure
  • State-space completeness (S, O, A, pi)
  • Matrix dimension consistency
  • Cross-reference integrity

docs.title: 3. Validate a bundle directory instead
docs.text:
If you have a run output directory (from cogant translate):

cogant validate ./output

COGANT looks for gnn_package/ inside and validates it, or falls back to lightweight bundle.json structure checks.

docs.title: 4. Interpret the score
docs.text:
VALID  score=87.5/100
errors=0  warnings=3

The score is 0-100. Warnings are informational; errors indicate spec violations that must be fixed.

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
Validating ./gnn_package
 VALID  score=92.0/100
 errors=0  warnings=1
 package: ./gnn_package
Warnings:
  - Missing optional field: model.gnn.json

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix INVALID with errors Read each error message; common issues are missing manifest fields or malformed markdown Not a file or directory Check the path exists No gnn_package/ and no bundle.json Ensure the directory contains either manifest.json + model.gnn.md or a bundle.json Score lower than expected Warnings reduce the score; fix them for a higher result

docs.title: Recipe 15: Visualizing Markov Blanket Partitions
docs.text: Goal: Generate a visual diagram of the Markov blanket partitions in a program graph. Time: ~5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed with viz extras: pip install "cogant[viz]"
  • Graphviz installed (brew install graphviz or apt install graphviz)

docs.title: 1. Translate the project
docs.text:
cogant translate ./my-project --output ./output --no-dynamic --layout-output

The --layout-output flag organizes artifacts into data/, diagrams/, figures/ subdirectories.

docs.title: 2. Generate PNG visualizations
docs.text:
cogant viz ./output

This walks the output directory and rasterizes every .mermaid, .mmd, .svg, and .dot file to PNG. It also generates program_graph.png from program_graph.json when present.

docs.title: 3. Inspect the blanket partitions
docs.text:
The program graph visualization color-codes nodes by their Markov blanket role:

Role Symbol Meaning mu Internal states Hidden state variables s Sensory states Observation/input nodes a Active states Action/output nodes eta External states Environment boundary

docs.title: 4. Find the generated PNGs
docs.text: find ./output -name "*.png" -type f

docs.title: 5. Export the state space for further analysis
docs.text:
cogant statespace ./my-project

This prints the count of states, observations, actions, and policies without writing files.

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
Rasterizing visualizations in /path/to/output
┌───────────┬───────┐
│ Category  │ Count │
├───────────┼───────┤
│ mermaid   │ 3     │
│ svg       │ 1     │
│ dot       │ 2     │
│ network   │ 1     │
└───────────┴───────┘
 Wrote 7 visualization files

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix cogant viz not found Ensure you installed cogant[viz]; run pip install "cogant[viz]" No PNGs generated Check the output directory contains .mermaid, .svg, or .dot files Graphviz errors Install graphviz: brew install graphviz (macOS) or apt install graphviz (Linux) Blank PNG The diagram may be empty if the repo has very few modules; check cogant scan output

docs.title: Recipe 16: Exporting Program Graph as PNG
docs.text: Goal: Rasterize all diagram artifacts in a COGANT output directory to PNG. Time: ~3 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed with viz extras: pip install "cogant[viz]"
  • Graphviz installed for .dot rendering

docs.title: 1. Run the pipeline first
docs.text: cogant translate ./my-project --output ./output --no-dynamic

docs.title: 2. Generate PNGs
docs.text:
cogant viz ./output

COGANT recursively walks the output directory and converts:

Source format Output .mermaid / .mmd <name>.png .svg <name>.png .dot <name>.png program_graph.json program_graph.png

docs.title: 3. Check the results
docs.text: ls ./output/**/*.png

docs.title: 4. Re-run after edits
docs.text:
cogant viz is idempotent. Existing PNGs are overwritten:

# Edit a .mermaid file, then regenerate
cogant viz ./output

docs.title: 5. Use with --layout-output for organized output
docs.text:
cogant translate ./my-project --output ./output --no-dynamic --layout-output
cogant viz ./output
ls ./output/figures/

The --layout-output flag moves diagram artifacts into a figures/ subdirectory before rasterization.

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
Rasterizing visualizations in /path/to/output
┌───────────┬───────┐
│ Category  │ Count │
├───────────┼───────┤
│ mermaid   │ 2     │
│ dot       │ 1     │
│ network   │ 1     │
└───────────┴───────┘
 Wrote 4 visualization files

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Path does not exist (exit code 2) Check the output directory path is correct Not a directory (exit code 2) cogant viz requires a directory, not a file 0 PNGs written The output directory has no renderable artifacts; ensure translate completed Missing graphviz .dot files need graphviz; install it or skip dot diagrams

docs.title: Recipe 17: Benchmarking COGANT Performance
docs.text: Goal: Measure pipeline wall-clock performance across several runs. Time: ~5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • A Python or JS/TS project directory

docs.title: 1. Run the benchmark
docs.text:
cogant benchmark ./my-project --iterations 5

COGANT runs the pipeline 5 times (skipping export and validate stages to focus on the translation core) and reports statistics.

docs.title: 2. Benchmark static analysis only
docs.text:
cogant benchmark ./my-project --iterations 5 --no-dynamic

The --no-dynamic flag skips coverage and trace analysis, measuring pure static-analysis throughput.

docs.title: 3. Compare before and after a change
docs.text:
# Baseline
cogant benchmark ./my-project -n 3 --no-dynamic > baseline.txt 2>&1

# Make changes, then re-benchmark
cogant benchmark ./my-project -n 3 --no-dynamic > after.txt 2>&1

diff baseline.txt after.txt

docs.title: 4. Estimate time for a new project
docs.text:
The init command provides a rough estimate:

cogant init ./new-project --check

This counts source files and estimates translate time at approximately 50 ms per file.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix High variance between runs Close background processes; use --no-dynamic for consistent results Unexpectedly slow Check file count with cogant scan; large repos take longer First run is much slower JIT/import warmup; discard the first iteration or add 1 extra

docs.title: Recipe 18: Filtering Results by Semantic Role
docs.text: Goal: Extract only nodes with a specific Active Inference role from COGANT output. Time: ~5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • jq installed for JSON processing

docs.title: 1. Translate the project
docs.text: cogant translate ./my-project --output ./output --no-dynamic

docs.title: 2. Inspect the program graph
docs.text:
jq 'keys' ./output/bundle.json

The translation results include nodes with semantic roles assigned.

docs.title: 3. Filter nodes by role using jq
docs.text:
Extract all nodes assigned the "internal state" (mu) role:

jq '[
  .stage_results.translate.nodes[]
  | select(.role == "mu")
  | {name: .name, role: .role, confidence: .confidence}
]' ./output/bundle.json

docs.title: 4. Filter for sensory nodes
docs.text:
jq '[
  .stage_results.translate.nodes[]
  | select(.role == "eta")
  | {name: .name, role: .role}
]' ./output/bundle.json

docs.title: 5. Get a role distribution summary
docs.text:
jq '
  .stage_results.translate.nodes
  | group_by(.role)
  | map({role: .[0].role, count: length})
  | sort_by(-.count)
' ./output/bundle.json

docs.title: 6. Export filtered nodes to a CSV
docs.text:
jq -r '
  .stage_results.translate.nodes[]
  | select(.role == "mu" or .role == "a")
  | [.name, .role, .confidence]
  | @csv
' ./output/bundle.json > active_nodes.csv

docs.title: 7. Use explain for deep inspection
docs.text:
For any node in the filtered list:

cogant explain ./my-project "NodeName" --format json

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
[
  {"name": "UserService", "role": "mu", "confidence": 0.87},
  {"name": "DatabasePool", "role": "mu", "confidence": 0.92},
  {"name": "CacheManager", "role": "mu", "confidence": 0.78}
]

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix null or empty result Check the correct JSON path; run jq 'keys' bundle.json to explore No nodes with a role The translation may have produced empty results; check cogant scan output jq syntax error Ensure jq is version 1.6+; test filters incrementally

docs.title: Recipe 19: Adding a Custom Translation Rule
docs.text: Goal: Extend COGANT's translation engine with a new rule. Time: ~15 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT source code checked out
  • Familiarity with the translation rule interface

docs.title: 1. Understand the rule interface
docs.text:
Translation rules live in cogant/py/cogant/translate/rules/. Each rule is a Python class that inspects a program-graph node and decides whether to assign it a semantic role.

A rule must implement:

class MyCustomRule:
    """One-line description shown in `cogant explain` output."""

    name: str = "my_custom_rule"
    priority: int = 50  # Lower fires first

    def evaluate(self, node, graph) -> RuleResult:
        """Return a RuleResult with role, confidence, and reason."""
        ...

docs.title: 2. Create the rule file
docs.text:
cat > cogant/py/cogant/translate/rules/my_custom_rule.py << 'EOF'
"""Custom rule: detect event-emitter classes as active states."""

from cogant.translate.rules.base import TranslationRule, RuleResult


class EventEmitterRule(TranslationRule):
    """Assign 'active state' (a) role to event-emitter classes."""

    name = "event_emitter"
    priority = 45  # Fire before generic class rules

    def evaluate(self, node, graph):
        # Check if the node is a class that emits events
        if node.kind != "class":
            return RuleResult.no_match()

        method_names = {m.name for m in node.methods}
        emitter_signals = {"emit", "dispatch", "publish", "notify"}

        if method_names & emitter_signals:
            return RuleResult(
                role="a",
                confidence=0.85,
                reason=f"Class has emitter methods: {method_names & emitter_signals}",
            )

        return RuleResult.no_match()
EOF

docs.title: 3. Register the rule
docs.text:
Add the rule to the plugin configuration in your pipeline config:

pipeline:
  plugins:
    translate:
      extra_rules:
        - cogant.translate.rules.my_custom_rule.EventEmitterRule

docs.title: 4. Test the rule
docs.text:
cogant translate ./my-project \
  --config cogant-config.yaml \
  --output ./output-custom-rules \
  --no-dynamic

docs.title: 5. Verify with explain
docs.text:
cogant explain ./my-project MyEventEmitter --format json

Check that event_emitter appears in the rules_fired list.

docs.title: 6. Compare with and without the custom rule
docs.text:
cogant translate ./my-project --output ./output-default --no-dynamic
cogant diff ./output-default ./output-custom-rules

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text: The cogant explain output shows the custom rule as FIRED with the assigned role and confidence score.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix Rule not firing Check priority is low enough to fire before competing rules Import error Ensure the module path in extra_rules matches the file location Confidence too low to appear Lower the confidence_threshold in the pipeline config Rule fires on wrong nodes Add more specific guards in evaluate (check node.kind, method names, etc.)

docs.title: Recipe 20: Exporting a Training Dataset for ML
docs.text: Goal: Export COGANT analysis results as a structured dataset for machine learning. Time: ~10 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed
  • jq installed
  • One or more translated repositories

docs.title: 1. Translate a project
docs.text: cogant translate ./my-project --output ./output --no-dynamic

docs.title: 2. Export the bundle as JSON
docs.text: cogant export-gnn ./output/bundle.json --output ./export --format json

docs.title: 3. Extract node features
docs.text:
Create a node-level dataset with features and labels:

jq '[
  .stage_results.translate.nodes[]
  | {
      name: .name,
      kind: .kind,
      role: .role,
      confidence: .confidence,
      in_degree: (.edges_in // [] | length),
      out_degree: (.edges_out // [] | length),
      method_count: (.methods // [] | length),
      has_state: (.has_state // false)
    }
]' ./output/bundle.json > nodes_dataset.json

docs.title: 4. Convert to CSV
docs.text:
jq -r '
  ["name","kind","role","confidence","in_degree","out_degree","method_count","has_state"],
  (.[] | [.name, .kind, .role, .confidence, .in_degree, .out_degree, .method_count, .has_state])
  | @csv
' nodes_dataset.json > nodes_dataset.csv

docs.title: 5. Extract edge features
docs.text:
jq '[
  .stage_results.graph.edges[]
  | {
      source: .source,
      target: .target,
      kind: .kind,
      weight: (.weight // 1.0)
    }
]' ./output/bundle.json > edges_dataset.json

docs.title: 6. Batch-export from multiple repos
docs.text:
for repo in ./repos/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$repo")
  cogant translate "$repo" --output "./batch/$name" --no-dynamic 2>/dev/null

  jq --arg repo "$name" '[
    .stage_results.translate.nodes[]
    | . + {repo: $repo}
  ]' "./batch/$name/bundle.json"
done | jq -s 'add' > combined_nodes.json

docs.title: 7. Generate adjacency matrices
docs.text:
jq '{
  nodes: [.stage_results.graph.nodes | keys[]],
  edges: [
    .stage_results.graph.edges[]
    | [.source, .target, (.weight // 1.0)]
  ]
}' ./output/bundle.json > adjacency.json

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
nodes_dataset.csv:

"name","kind","role","confidence","in_degree","out_degree","method_count","has_state"
"UserService","class","mu",0.87,3,5,4,true
"auth_handler","function","a",0.72,1,2,0,false
"db_connection","module","eta",0.91,0,3,0,false

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix null values in jq output Use // default to provide fallback values Empty dataset Ensure cogant translate completed without errors Missing fields COGANT's JSON schema may vary by version; inspect with jq 'keys' first Large files Filter by role or confidence threshold before export

docs.title: AGENTS.md — Cookbook module
docs.text: Short, self-contained, copy-paste-friendly recipes for COGANT workflows. Each recipe answers a single "how do I..." question and runs end-to-end in 2-15 minutes. The cookbook is where readers land when they already know the tool exists and want to get a specific job done.

docs.title: Purpose and ownership
docs.text: Recipes, not tutorials or reference. If a page grows into a multi-hour walkthrough, move it to ../tutorials/. If a page becomes a schema or API dump, move the reference chunks into ../reference/ or ../api/ and link back. Owned by whoever is editing the CLI / user-facing workflows.

docs.title: File map
docs.text: File Purpose Update trigger README.md TOC, numbering policy, non-numbered recipe registry Any time a recipe is added, removed, renamed, or changes difficulty AGENTS.md This file — maintenance rules When numbering, non-numbered-recipe, or ownership policy changes 01_scan_basic.md – 20_dataset.md Numbered recipes, read the README table for descriptions When the CLI, pipeline, or exporter they demonstrate changes analyze_a_flask_app.md Pre-numbering Flask walkthrough — kept stable for inbound links When the Flask example itself is moved or the CLI contract changes custom_translation_rules.md Pre-numbering custom-rules recipe; use 19_extend_rules.md for new work Only to fix factual errors; new content goes in the numbered recipe interpret_gnn_output.md Pre-numbering GNN interpretation recipe; use 03_explain_node.md for new work Only to fix factual errors; new content goes in the numbered recipe

docs.title: Adding a new recipe
docs.text:
1. Pick the next free NN prefix (current max is 20). Reserve your number with a draft PR before writing, so two contributors do not collide.
  2. Use a short, lower-case, underscore-separated slug (for example 21_custom_exporter.md).
  3. Open with a one-sentence statement of the outcome ("By the end of this recipe you will..."), followed by prerequisites, steps, and expected output. Prefer copy-pasteable shell blocks and cogant CLI invocations over prose.
  4. Add a row to the ## Contents table in README.md and, if the recipe belongs in the onboarding spine, mention it in ## Recommended Reading Order as well.
  5. Reference the relevant CLI / API / rules pages with ../cli/README.md, ../api/README.md, ../rules/README.md rather than re-explaining them.

docs.title: Known gotchas
docs.text:
• Three non-numbered recipes (analyze_a_flask_app.md, custom_translation_rules.md, interpret_gnn_output.md) overlap topically with numbered recipes. Do not delete them — external docs and blog posts may link to them by slug. If a consolidation pass happens later, keep a stub with a redirect note at minimum.
  • The cookbook and ../tutorials/ overlap deliberately: cookbook entries are outcome-first and short; tutorial entries are pedagogy-first and long. If you cannot decide, write the cookbook recipe first — it is easier to promote a recipe into a tutorial than to split a tutorial into recipes.

docs.title: Recipe: Analyze a Flask App
docs.text:
Goal: Run the full COGANT pipeline against the canonical six-module Flask fixture and read the GNN bundle.

This is a short, copy-pasteable recipe. For the full narrative — node and edge counts, role distribution tables, and per-module commentary — see Tutorial 3: Flask walkthrough and the deep-dive in flask.md.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• COGANT installed (uv sync from a checkout, or pip install cogant).
  • The repo's bundled fixture at examples/real_world/flask_app/. It contains six Python modules totalling 853 lines: __init__.py, app.py, config.py, models.py, services.py, utils.py.

docs.title: Step 1 — translate
docs.text:
uv run cogant translate examples/real_world/flask_app \
    --output output/flask_app \
    --layout-output

This runs the default stages=["ingest", "static", "normalize", "graph", "translate", "statespace", "process", "export", "validate"] pipeline. Expect a 100 / 100 validator score on a clean checkout.

docs.title: Step 2 — validate
docs.text:
uv run cogant validate output/flask_app/gnn_package

Expected output:

GNN validation: output/flask_app/gnn_package
  Score:    100.0 / 100
  Errors:   0
  Warnings: 0

docs.title: Step 3 — read the bundle
docs.text:
The bundle directory output/flask_app/gnn_package/ contains:

File What's in it model.gnn.md Canonical GNN markdown — human-readable role table. model.gnn.json Same content, machine-readable. A.json, B.json, C.json, D.json The four generative-model matrices. manifest.json Bundle metadata, validator score, edge / node counts.

For a row-by-row walkthrough of A.json, B.json, C.json, D.json, see Tutorial 5: Reading the A / B / C / D matrices.

docs.title: Step 4 — programmatic equivalent
docs.text:
The same pipeline through the Python API:

from cogant import PipelineRunner
from cogant.api.pipeline import PipelineConfig

runner = PipelineRunner()
config = PipelineConfig(output_dir="output/flask_app")
bundle = runner.run("./examples/real_world/flask_app", config)

assert not bundle.errors
print(bundle.repo_summary())
bundle.save_json("output/flask_app/bundle.json")

  • PipelineRunner API — every option used above.
  • docs/api/static.md — what the static stage does to the six modules.

docs.title: Recipe: Custom Translation Rules
docs.text:
Goal: Write, register, test, and ship a new TranslationRule so the fixpoint engine emits your role assignment alongside the 22 built-in rules.

This is the short, copy-pasteable recipe. For the rationale, the precedence rules, and a fully-explained example (the read-only-cache rule) see Tutorial 4: Writing a custom translation rule.

docs.title: When to write a rule vs. configure an existing one
docs.text:
• Configure existing — if you only need to retune confidence tiers or keyword patterns, prefer the configuration knobs documented in the translate API page. Don't fork.
  • New rule — if you need a new graph pattern that none of the five families (structural / semantic / behavioral / control / resilience) matches, write a TranslationRule subclass.

docs.title: Step 1 — pick a family and a priority
docs.text: Rules live in py/cogant/translate/rules/{family}.py. Lower priority numbers fire later — the conflict-resolution pass uses priority + confidence to break ties. Pick a slot that does not collide with the built-ins (see py/cogant/translate/rules/__init__.py for the registered priorities).

docs.title: Step 2 — subclass TranslationRule
docs.text:
from cogant.schemas.core import NodeKind, EdgeKind
from cogant.schemas.graph import ProgramGraph
from cogant.schemas.semantic import SemanticMapping, MappingKind, ConfidenceTier
from cogant.graph.queries import GraphQuery
from cogant.translate.engine import TranslationRule, RuleExplanation


class MyRule(TranslationRule):
    name = "MyRule"
    priority = 55  # see step 1

    def matches(self, graph: ProgramGraph, query: GraphQuery) -> bool:
        # Cheap pre-filter — return False fast.
        return any(n.kind is NodeKind.CLASS for n in graph.nodes)

    def apply(self, graph: ProgramGraph, query: GraphQuery) -> list[SemanticMapping]:
        mappings: list[SemanticMapping] = []
        # … emit SemanticMapping(kind=MappingKind.OBSERVATION, …) …
        return mappings

    def explain(self, mapping: SemanticMapping) -> RuleExplanation:
        return RuleExplanation(
            rule_name=self.name,
            evidence=[...],
            confidence_reason="...",
        )

docs.title: Step 3 — register
docs.text: Add the class to the family's __all__ list and to the rule registry in py/cogant/translate/rules/__init__.py. The engine auto-discovers registered rules at startup.

docs.title: Step 4 — test (no mocks)
docs.text:
Drop a real fixture into tests/fixtures/ (or under examples/zoo/ if it's useful as a public example) and write a real-data assertion:

from pathlib import Path
from cogant import Session

def test_my_rule_fires_on_fixture():
    session = Session.from_target(Path("tests/fixtures/my_rule_target"))
    session.extract_static()
    session.build_graph()
    session.translate_to_gnn()
    mappings = session.semantic_mappings()
    assert any(m.rule_name == "MyRule" for m in mappings)

docs.title: Step 5 — ship
docs.text: If the rule is project-internal: commit it under py/cogant/translate/rules/. If you want to ship it as a third-party package, expose it via the plugin entry point documented in plugin_api.md.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Tutorial 4: Writing a custom translation rule — full read-only-cache walkthrough.
  • docs/api/translate.md — every public symbol your rule will touch.
  • Recipe 19: Adding a custom translation rule — the numbered custom-rule recipe.
  • Recipe 3: Explain a single node — using RuleExplanation from the CLI.

docs.title: Recipe: Interpret GNN Output
docs.text:
Goal: Take an exported GNN bundle, open the four matrices, and explain what each row and column means in terms of the source code that produced it.

This is the short recipe. For the full mathematical narrative — the p(o, s, a) factorization, the per-edge derivation, and a worked example on both the calculator and flask_app fixtures — see Tutorial 5: Reading the A / B / C / D matrices.

docs.title: What's in a GNN bundle
docs.text:
After running cogant translate <target> --output <out>, you get <out>/gnn_package/:

File Shape / Format Source A.json [n_obs × n_states] Likelihood P(observation \| hidden_state) B.json [n_states × n_states × n_actions] Transition P(s' \| s, a) C.json [n_obs] Log-preference over observations D.json [n_states] Initial-state prior P(s_0) model.gnn.md Markdown Human-readable role table model.gnn.json JSON Same content, machine-readable manifest.json JSON Validator score, edge / node counts

The matrix builder lives in cogant.gnn.matrices; the validator lives in cogant.gnn.validator.

docs.title: Step 1 — generate a small bundle
docs.text:
uv run cogant translate examples/zoo/04_pomdp_minimal \
    --output output/pomdp_minimal --layout-output
ls output/pomdp_minimal/gnn_package/

docs.title: Step 2 — read the A matrix (likelihood)
docs.text:
import json

A = json.load(open("output/pomdp_minimal/gnn_package/A.json"))
for row in A["matrix"]:
    print(["{:.2f}".format(x) for x in row])

Each row is an observation modality; each column is a hidden-state factor. A 1.0 means this exported observation receives all of the normalized likelihood mass for that hidden-state column in the emitted matrix; it is a structural edge-evidence statement, not proof that the observation is empirically fully informative about runtime behavior. Rows are softmax-normalized.

docs.title: Step 3 — read the B matrix (transition)
docs.text:
B = json.load(open("output/pomdp_minimal/gnn_package/B.json"))
print("shape:", B["shape"])  # [n_states, n_states, n_actions]

B[s', s, a] is the probability of transitioning from s to s' under action a. Each B[:, :, a] slice is a column-stochastic matrix.

docs.title: Step 4 — read C and D
docs.text:
C = json.load(open("output/pomdp_minimal/gnn_package/C.json"))  # log-preferences over observations
D = json.load(open("output/pomdp_minimal/gnn_package/D.json"))  # prior over initial hidden states
print("C:", C["vector"])
print("D:", D["vector"])

C is in log-space — apply softmax(-C) to get the preferred-observation distribution. D is already a probability vector.

docs.title: Step 5 — validate the bundle
docs.text:
uv run cogant validate output/pomdp_minimal/gnn_package

A clean fixture should score 100 / 100. If not, see Recipe 14: Validating a hand-written GNN against AII spec.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
• Why are some rows in A all zeros? — that observation modality has no READS / OBSERVES / DEPENDS_ON edges in the program graph. Either the source genuinely doesn't observe that state, or you're missing a static analysis pass — re-run with --verbose and check the static stage output.
  • Why does B have only one action slice? — the cogant.translate engine produced exactly one ACTION mapping. Add an actor class or re-run with a relaxed ActionRule keyword set.
  • What does the validator score actually measure? — see cogant.gnn.validator.

docs.text:

  • docs/api/gnn.md — the matrix builder, runner, validator, and JSON exporter.
  • Recipe 14: Validating a GNN — what the score 0–100 means.
